ui.none: No ticket matches. Try another word or category.

causes.1: Label roll empty or not seated correctly.
causes.2: Print job stuck in the queue on the Mac.
causes.3: Printer off or its cable unplugged.

checks.1: Display or LED: error or paper out?
checks.2: Print queue on the Mac: paused or stuck job? (lpstat -p)
checks.3: Does the printer answer a ping? (ping 10.2.50.22)
checks.4: Print a test label from the printer itself.

label-printer.solution: Reload and calibrate the roll, clear the queue, resume the printer. If it still fails, use the spare: same model, same settings.

scan-folder.symptom: “Scans no longer arrive in the shared folder.”

causes.1: Password of the scan account changed or expired.
causes.2: File server not reachable (VPN or server down).
causes.3: Permissions on the folder changed.

checks.1: Error message on the printer display.
checks.2: Does the shared folder open on a Mac in the same clinic?
checks.3: Scan account in the directory: locked or expired?

scan-folder.solution: Give the scan account a long password that does not expire, stored in the password manager, then send a test scan.

causes.1: Network cable loose or switch port down.
causes.2: Internet line down: the terminal only talks to the payment provider.
causes.3: Terminal needs a restart or an update.

checks.1: Link LED at the terminal and at the switch port.
checks.2: Connection test on the terminal.
checks.3: Do other devices in the clinic reach the internet?
checks.4: Firewall dashboard: does the terminal have an address in VLAN 40?

card-terminal.solution: Reseat the cable and restart the terminal. If the line is down, LTE takes over; until then use the second terminal or cash.
card-terminal.warning: Do not plug the terminal into another socket: only VLAN 40 ports reach the payment provider.

wifi-treatment.symptom: “The Wi-Fi in treatment room 2 keeps dropping.”

causes.1: Access point overloaded or faulty.
causes.2: Weak coverage: X-ray room shielding or thick walls.
causes.3: The Mac holds on to a distant access point instead of roaming.

checks.1: Which access point is the Mac on, and how strong is the signal?
checks.2: Cloud dashboard: clients and errors on that access point.
checks.3: Everywhere in the room, or only in one corner?
checks.4: Same problem on a second device?

wifi-treatment.solution: Restart or replace the access point. For a coverage hole, measure and add or move an access point instead of turning up the power.

file-share.symptom: “My Mac can't open the shared folder.”

causes.1: VPN tunnel to headquarters down.
causes.2: File server stopped or overloaded.
causes.3: Saved login no longer valid (password changed).

checks.1: Can colleagues in the same clinic open it?
checks.2: Tunnel status in the firewall dashboard.
checks.3: Does the file server answer? (nc -vz 10.0.70.21 445)
checks.4: Disconnect the share and connect again with the current password.

file-share.solution: Reconnect with the current password. If the whole clinic is affected, fix the tunnel or the server first.

xray-archive.symptom: “The X-ray images don't show up in the archive.”

causes.1: Image archive (PACS) stopped or its disk is full.
causes.2: VPN tunnel down: images wait on the X-ray PC.
causes.3: Wrong destination in the X-ray software after an update.

checks.1: Send queue on the X-ray PC: images waiting?
checks.2: DICOM echo from the X-ray PC to the archive.
checks.3: Tunnel status in the firewall dashboard.
checks.4: Archive server: service running, disk space left?

xray-archive.solution: Fix the cause, then resend the waiting images. Never delete images on the X-ray PC before the archive has confirmed them.

lab-results.symptom: “The lab results don't appear in the patient file.”

causes.1: Lab interface server stopped.
causes.2: Analyzer sends to an old address.
causes.3: Patient number typed differently on the analyzer.

checks.1: Analyzer log: was the result sent?
checks.2: Lab interface server: running, last message received?
checks.3: Does the patient number match the practice software?
checks.4: Import errors in the practice software?

lab-results.solution: Restart the interface or correct the address, then resend from the analyzer. Fix mismatched patient numbers by hand.

vpn-down.symptom: “Nothing from headquarters works: shared folders, X-ray images.”

causes.1: VPN tunnel down (key, address or firmware).
causes.2: Internet line down.
causes.3: Problem at headquarters: other clinics are affected too.

checks.1: Does the internet work (practice software, websites)?
checks.2: Tunnel status in the firewall dashboard.
checks.3: Do other clinics have the same problem?

vpn-down.solution: Restart the tunnel from the dashboard. Card payments and the practice software keep working in the meantime.

causes.1: Line degraded, or the clinic runs on the LTE backup.
causes.2: A large upload or update fills the line.
causes.3: Problem at the provider.

checks.1: Firewall dashboard: which line is active, how busy is it?
checks.2: Top talkers: which device uses the bandwidth?
checks.3: Speed test against the contract.

internet-slow.solution: Stop or reschedule the large transfer. If the line itself is bad, report it with measurements; updates run after opening hours.

causes.1: Internet line busy and voice not prioritised.
causes.2: Faulty cable or switch port at the phone.
causes.3: Problem at the telephone provider.

checks.1: One phone or all phones?
checks.2: Line usage during the call.
checks.3: Error counters on the phone's switch port.

voip-quality.solution: Make sure VLAN 60 is prioritised on the firewall and switch. If only one phone is affected, replace its cable or port.

guest-wifi.symptom: “Pet owners can't get onto the guest Wi-Fi.”

causes.1: Address pool full because leases are long.
causes.2: Guest password changed but the sign was not.
causes.3: Access point in the waiting room is off.

checks.1: Does a phone get an address, not 169.254.x.x?
checks.2: Firewall dashboard: free addresses in the guest pool.
checks.3: Is the waiting room access point online?

guest-wifi.solution: Shorten the lease time (for example one hour) and enlarge the pool if needed. The staff Wi-Fi is separate and not affected.

locked-out.symptom: “I'm locked out and can't log in.”

causes.1: Too many wrong attempts, often an old password saved on a phone.
causes.2: Password expired.
causes.3: Account disabled by mistake.

checks.1: Verify who is calling: call back on a known number.
checks.2: Directory: locked, expired or disabled?
checks.3: Which device keeps trying the old password?

locked-out.solution: Unlock, or set a temporary password that must be changed at the next login, and remove the old one from the phone. Never send passwords by e-mail.

causes.1: Request comes too late or without a role.
causes.2: No Mac assigned in the MDM.
causes.3: Rights copied from a colleague instead of from the role.

checks.1: Get the role from the clinic manager: reception, vet or back office.
checks.2: Create the account from the role template, with MFA.
checks.3: Assign a Mac in the MDM; it sets itself up on first start.
checks.4: Create the user in the practice software with the role's rights.

onboarding.solution: Everything is ready before day one, plus a one-page start sheet: login, MFA, Wi-Fi, who to call.

causes.1: Accounts stay active after the last day.
causes.2: Shared passwords the person knew are not changed.
causes.3: Devices are not returned or not wiped.

checks.1: Disable the account at the end of the last working day.
checks.2: Remove access to practice software, telephone system and groups.
checks.3: Change shared passwords the person knew.
checks.4: Collect the Mac and wipe it from the MDM.

offboarding.solution: Work through the offboarding checklist on the same day. Keep mailbox and files for the retention period, then delete them.

update-broke.symptom: “Since last night's update, a program won't start.”

causes.1: The app is not yet compatible with the new macOS.
causes.2: Update installed only half-way.
causes.3: Permissions reset by the update.

checks.1: One Mac, or all Macs with the same update?
checks.2: MDM: which version, installed when?
checks.3: Release notes and vendor support of the app.

update-broke.solution: Pause the update in the MDM, work in the browser or on another Mac, install the fixed app version. Next time: pilot group first.

disk-full.symptom: “My Mac says the disk is almost full.”

causes.1: Large downloads or images saved locally.
causes.2: Old caches and installers.
causes.3: A sync folder keeps everything offline.

checks.1: System Settings, Storage: what uses the space?
checks.2: Downloads and Desktop folders.
checks.3: MDM: disk usage report of all Macs.

disk-full.solution: Move files to the shared folder, empty Downloads and Trash, limit offline sync. Patient data does not belong on the Mac anyway.

cert-expired.symptom: “The browser warns ‘connection not private’ when I open X-ray images.”

causes.1: The server certificate has expired.
causes.2: Date and time on the Mac are wrong.
causes.3: A new Mac lacks the internal root certificate.

checks.1: Certificate details: expiry date and issuer.
checks.2: Date and time on the Mac.
checks.3: Same warning on other Macs?

cert-expired.solution: Renew the certificate on the server; do not click through the warning. If only one Mac is affected, push the root certificate via MDM.

mdm-not-enrolled.symptom: “The new Mac doesn't get its apps or Wi-Fi.”

causes.1: Mac not bought through the channel that registers it for automatic enrolment.
causes.2: Not yet assigned to the MDM server.
causes.3: Set up without internet, so the remote management step was skipped.

checks.1: Did the setup assistant show the remote management screen?
checks.2: Is the serial number in the business device portal?
checks.3: MDM: is the device listed and assigned to a profile?

mdm-not-enrolled.solution: Assign the serial number to the MDM, erase the Mac and set it up again with internet. Buy future Macs through the approved channel.

double-charge.symptom: “The customer says the card was charged twice.”

causes.1: The terminal waited too long for an answer, and the payment was started again.
causes.2: The first payment went through, but the receipt did not print.
causes.3: Both terminals were used for the same invoice.

checks.1: Print the terminal journal: are there two approved payments?
checks.2: Compare amount, time and the last digits of the card.
checks.3: Has the daily closing already run?
checks.4: Slow internet at that time? Check the firewall dashboard.

double-charge.solution: Cancel the duplicate on the same terminal before the daily closing. After the closing, refund it by bank transfer and note it on the invoice.
double-charge.warning: Never start a payment again while the first one has no clear result. Check the journal first.

card-brand-declined.symptom: “girocard works, but credit cards are declined.”

causes.1: That card brand is not active in the merchant contract or on the terminal.
causes.2: The provider has an outage for one card network.
causes.3: A problem with this one card: limit or block by the bank.

checks.1: Does it fail for every card of that brand, or for just one?
checks.2: Note the error code the terminal shows.
checks.3: Check the provider status page.
checks.4: Did a terminal update or a contract change happen recently?

card-brand-declined.solution: Only one card fails: the customer contacts their bank. A whole brand fails: call the provider with the terminal ID (TID) and the error code.

payment-offline.symptom: “The internet is down and LTE too. No card payments.”

causes.1: Primary line and LTE backup are down at the same time.
causes.2: The LTE SIM is out of data or not active.
causes.3: The firewall itself is down, so no line is used.

checks.1: Firewall dashboard: status of WAN1 and WAN2.
checks.2: Does the LTE router show signal and an active SIM?
checks.3: Is it just this clinic? Ask the other sites.

payment-offline.solution: The terminal needs a connection to approve a payment. Take cash or issue an invoice, and fix the lines with the provider.
payment-offline.warning: Never write down card numbers or PINs as a workaround. That breaks the card payment rules.

payment-blocked.symptom: “Since the firewall change the terminal says ‘host unreachable’.”

causes.1: The payment rule for VLAN 40 was changed or overwritten.
causes.2: The provider uses new addresses, but the rule allows old IPs only.
causes.3: TLS inspection now decrypts the payment traffic and breaks it.

checks.1: Firewall log: blocked connections from VLAN 40?
checks.2: Compare the rule with the site template.
checks.3: Is VLAN 40 excluded from TLS inspection?

payment-blocked.solution: Restore the rule from the template and allow the provider by its documented host names. Keep VLAN 40 out of TLS inspection.
payment-blocked.warning: Every firewall change at a clinic ends with a test payment, before staff go home.

end-of-day.symptom: “The terminal asks for a daily closing and holds payments.”

causes.1: The daily closing was not run yesterday.
causes.2: The closing started but did not finish: connection lost.
causes.3: The automatic closing is set to a time when the terminal is off.

checks.1: Terminal menu: date of the last successful closing.
checks.2: Is the terminal online right now?
checks.3: Which closing time is set?

end-of-day.solution: Run the closing by hand and keep the closing receipt. Set the automatic closing to a time when the terminal is on.

terminal-swap.symptom: “The card terminal is broken. A replacement has arrived.”

causes.1: The new terminal is plugged into a port that is not in VLAN 40.
causes.2: The terminal was not set up with the provider, so cards are declined.
causes.3: The test payment is not cancelled and stays on the statement.

checks.1: Plug it into the same switch port as the old one (VLAN 40).
checks.2: Run the setup the provider describes; note the terminal ID.
checks.3: Make a small test payment and cancel it.
checks.4: Send the old terminal back as the provider asks.

terminal-swap.solution: Swap, set up, test payment, cancel. Note the new terminal ID in the inventory.

no-ip.symptom: “The new laptop has no network, the old ones work.”

causes.1: The address pool of the staff network is full.
causes.2: Devices with private (random) MAC addresses use up many leases.
causes.3: The laptop is in the wrong Wi-Fi, for example the guest network.

checks.1: Does the Mac show a 169.254.x.x address?
checks.2: Firewall: DHCP leases in VLAN 20, how many are free?
checks.3: Which Wi-Fi is the laptop in?

no-ip.solution: Remove old leases and shorten the lease time; enlarge the pool if needed. Private phones belong in the guest Wi-Fi.

phishing.symptom: “I entered my password on a page from an e-mail.”

causes.1: An e-mail with a “shared document” or parcel link.
causes.2: A login page that looks real, on a different domain.
causes.3: An MFA prompt approved without logging in yourself.

checks.1: Reset the password and sign out all sessions at once.
checks.2: Sign-in log: logins from unknown places?
checks.3: Mailbox: new forwarding or inbox rules?
checks.4: Warn the team and block the sender and the link.

phishing.solution: Thank the person for reporting fast; that limits the damage. If personal data was accessed, the 72-hour reporting rule may apply.
phishing.warning: Do not delete the e-mail before IT has seen it. It shows where the link led.
